question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group Fewer Than Ten
question.problem: How many made-up $3$-letter words can be made using only $5$ vowels, where each vowel cannot appear in the word more than once?
question.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $5$ vowels, so $n=5.$ We want to select $3$ of those vowels to make-up a $3$-letter word, so we have $r=3.$ 

Therefore, the number of different made-up words is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{5}{P}_{3} & =\frac{5!}{(5-3)!} \\  & =\frac{5!}{2!} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{2!}}{\cancel{2!}} \\  & =5\cdot 4\cdot 3 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$
